title: dynamic batching: improved sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization (v2)
author: Ivy Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce wasted token compute caused by naive batching across variable sequence lengths. Existing dynamic-batching groups by arrival time which often mixes short and long sequences resulting in excessive padding and KV cache churn. This PR implements a second-generation sequence-length bucketing heuristic and padding minimization strategy integrated with the continuous batching pipeline and scheduler.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight bucketing layer that assigns an incoming request to one of N sequence-length buckets (configurable, default 8) before batching. Buckets are maintained with per-bucket timers to preserve latency SLOs. 2) Add padding-aware batch assembler: when the scheduler builds a batch, it prefers candidates from the same bucket and prioritizes items that reduce max-seqlen padding. 3) Integrate bucketing signals into the runtime kernel selector so that kernel shapes are chosen for the batch's effective sequence length distribution. 4) Reduce KV cache thrash: requests staying within the same bucket reuse warm KV cache entries where safe; we added an eviction policy that is bucket-aware. 5) Metrics/observability: new histograms for padding_ratio, bucket_fill_time, and kv_cache_miss_by_bucket. 6) Added deterministic unit and integration tests and benchmark harness updates.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR comments - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration e2e runs in benchmark-lab - [x] CI green - [x] Performance regression checks run - [x] Docs note for runtime tuning

Performance: On internal conversational workload (mix of short prompts and long context) we see: - End-to-end per-token GPU compute reduction: ~12-18% median - 99th percentile latency improvement for tail workloads with mixed seq lengths: 8-12% - KV cache miss rate down by 9% on average - In dedicated workload with heavy short-sequence traffic, effective throughput improvement up to 22% when using 8 buckets vs baseline single-bucket dynamic batching.

Compatibility: defaults preserve existing behavior when buckets=1. Bucketing is opt-in via runtime config and feature-flagged for a 2-week canary rollout on dedicated clusters. Backwards-compatible on wire/API level.
commits_summary: 8 commits: initial bucketing interface; padding-aware batch assembler; kernel selector integration; KV cache eviction updates; metrics and dashboards; unit/integration tests; docs and config; follow-up perf tweaks
review_comments: Rohan Patel: Please clarify how bucket timers interact with existing latency SLO enforcement; are we introducing any latency tail regressions?\nIvy Chen: Buckets have per-bucket max_wait timers derived from the global SLO and a configurable bucket_latency_factor; in tests we ensured no tail regressions for 95/99 percentiles and added metrics to monitor bucket_fill_time.

Maria Gonzalez: Kernel selector changes look invasive — can we keep a fallback to previous selector when experimental flag off?\nIvy Chen: Added a compatibility path; selector consults runtime_config.enable_bucketed_kernels and falls back to old selection if false. Unit tests cover both branches.

Ethan Brooks: KV cache reuse across buckets seems risky for ctx-misaligned models (different key shapes). How do we guard correctness?\nIvy Chen: We only reuse KV entries for buckets with identical model sharding and quantization profiles; we compare a fast bucket signature before reuse. Added assertive checks in debug builds and an opt-out policy for private deployments.

Rohan Patel: Could you add an example config for tuning buckets for low-latency vs high-throughput?\nIvy Chen: Added quickstart and runtime_config examples under console/docs and helm values; included in this PR.
Maria Gonzalez (approval): LGTM after CI fixes; performance numbers validated in benchmark-lab.
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching heuristics: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization reduce wasted compute and KV cache thrash; default remains unchanged. Configurable bucket count and latency tuning options added to runtime_config.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout plan: enable feature flag on 5% of dedicated clusters for 48h, monitor padding_ratio and bucket_fill_time histograms, then increment to 25% if no regressions. Fallback: flip feature flag off to revert to single-bucket behavior.
changelog_entry: Added sequence-length bucketing to dynamic batching with padding minimization; reduces padding overhead and KV cache misses; configurable via runtime_config.runtime.batching.buckets
security_impact: low - no new external surface; bucket metadata kept in-memory and not logged by default
qa_notes: Test scenarios included: pure-short, pure-long, mixed arrivals, adversarial sequence arrival patterns. Regression tests added to CI.
